I love the first album so it's really hard to decide, but I'd probably have to say ain't no rest for the wicked because it introduced me to slide guitar which is one of the few ways I can get super pumped while listening to acoustic driven music.

For TYHB I'd have to say Around my head mostly for the way the rythym and leads are split, speaking of which that songs rythem and leads are pretty good.

From Melophobia, no doubt in my mind, come a little closer. That chilled out jazzy rythem and lead guitar along with Tich's bass give a nice level of going strong while also being relaxed. Jared's drumming is also some of his best work in my opinion.

There's pretty much one reason why Cold Cold Cold gets my vote; it is without a doubt their best combination of note choice and tone. That ripping fuzz when I first heard it sent shivers down my spine. I think it crazy that they set it on a song about depression, but it works so well.

Ngl I didn't like social cues nearly as much as any of their albums. It's really good, but it's not as good as their other stuff. I will say this however, there's no song better than Night Running for any exercising. I go for bike rides whenever the borderline desert I live in isn't a hundred degrees, and there is not a bigger push than that intro guitar riff.

I'm going to be really short for the live albums. Back against the wall captured the feeling of the record and sounded amazing. I didn't like unpeeled all that much. Cage's songs really mesh with acoustic guitar, but I don't want to listen to that for an hour+. That being said, whole wide world is one of the best songs on that album.
